metadata.title: Countercyclical pricing dashboard critique
metadata.source: Retail scanner data, U.S. supermarkets and drug stores
metadata.winter_definition: Winter = October, November, December, January, February for this soup case.

redesignedSequence.title: Executive question
redesignedSequence.question: Is Progresso pricing against the seasonal demand cycle?
redesignedSequence.decision: Decide whether the pattern deserves a pricing test.

redesignedSequence.title: Demand baseline
redesignedSequence.question: When is category demand strongest and weakest?
redesignedSequence.visual: Monthly volume indexed to January plus active store counts.
redesignedSequence.decision: Separate seasonal demand from price action.

redesignedSequence.title: Price response
redesignedSequence.question: Does price rise when demand weakens?
redesignedSequence.visual: Progresso and Campbell monthly price lines.

redesignedSequence.title: Market heterogeneity
redesignedSequence.question: Is the pattern national or regional?
redesignedSequence.visual: Region small multiples for price and share.
redesignedSequence.decision: Avoid one national recommendation if regions differ.

redesignedSequence.title: Statistical preview
redesignedSequence.question: How steep is the price-volume association?
redesignedSequence.visual: Log price vs log volume scatter with coefficient intervals.
redesignedSequence.decision: Bridge to later elasticity and identification chapters.

redesignedSequence.title: Next test
redesignedSequence.question: What would we need to know before changing price?
redesignedSequence.visual: Action panel: descriptive pattern, causal limit, recommended experiment or quasi-experimental design.
redesignedSequence.decision: Do not treat the dashboard as causal proof.

dashboardRules: Start with the decision question, not the available charts.
Label panels as monitor, diagnose, or decide.
Put coverage and caveats near the charts they affect.
End with the next test or decision, not with another descriptive chart.
